headline: Westpac's APRA Level 2 CET1 capital ratio rose 4 bps to 12.53% at September 2025 from 12.49% at September 2024. The increase from net profit ($6,966m ex Notable Items, down slightly from $7,106m in FY24) less payment of the 2024 final and 2025 interim ordinary dividends (153 cents per share total, up from 151 cents plus a 15-cent special dividend in FY24) and other reserve movements including lower capitalised software balances (down $261m to $2,414m) was largely offset by higher Total RWA of $450.0bn (up $12.6bn, mainly from lending growth of $12.6bn partly offset by data refinements of $5.9bn and IRRBB improvements of $2.0bn) and on-market share buybacks. The bank does not publish a full-year CET1 walk chart — only a half-on-half (Mar-25 to Sep-25) walk showing +80 bps from net profit, −58 bps from dividends, −7 bps from RWA, +16 bps from capital deductions/other, and −2 bps from capital return.

drivers.narrative: Net profit excluding Notable Items was $6,966m in FY25, down from $7,106m in FY24 (ev-26). The bank states the increase from net profit contributed to the CET1 ratio movement (ev-2). Earnings generated capital but were largely offset by dividends and RWA growth.

Total ordinary dividends were 153 cents per share in FY25 versus 151 cents plus a 15-cent special dividend in FY24 (ev-24, ev-25). The bank states the increase from net profit was less the payment of the 2024 final ordinary dividend and 2025 interim ordinary dividend (ev-2). DRP for the 2025 final dividend will be satisfied by third-party market purchases (ev-31).

Total RWA increased $12.6bn to $450.0bn from $437.4bn (ev-28). The RWA bridge (ev-33) shows: lending +$12.6bn, data refinement −$5.9bn, credit quality −$3.0bn, IRRBB −$2.0bn, FX translation −$1.8bn, counterparty credit & MTM −$0.7bn, market risk +$1.4bn, operational risk −$0.1bn. The bank states Total RWA increased mainly from higher IRRBB RWA (ev-2). Higher RWA diluted the CET1 ratio.

Other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances contributed to the CET1 ratio. Capitalised software decreased $261m (10%) to $2,414m from $2,675m, reflecting increased amortisation from completion of key projects including One Banking Platform and RBNZ outsourcing compliance (ev-20). The half-on-half walk attributes +16 bps to capital deductions and other items (ev-3).

On-market share buybacks reduced CET1. The half-on-half walk shows a −2 bps impact from capital return due to the on-market share buyback (ev-3). The bank states buybacks offset the CET1 ratio increase (ev-2). Full-year bps impact is not separately disclosed.

limitations: No full-year (Sep-24 to Sep-25) CET1 ratio walk chart is published by WBC — only a half-on-half (Mar-25 to Sep-25) walk is available. The half-on-half bars cannot be used as FY25 vs FY24 contributions per the task rules.
Driver contributions are unquantified in bps for the full-year comparison because the bank does not disclose them. Only the narrative direction and magnitude of drivers are stated.
The residual of 4 bps equals the total movement because individual drivers are not quantified — they sum to the delta only qualitatively.

The RWA bridge chart (ev-33) is primary for the task comparison but measures RWA in $m, not CET1 bps. Converting RWA $m changes to CET1 ratio bps requires the CET1 capital level as denominator and is not provided by the bank.
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.

evidence_records.quote: The Level 2 CET1 capital ratio was 12.53% at 30 September 2025, 4 basis points higher than 30 September 2024. The increase from net profit less the payment of 2024 final ordinary dividend and 2025 interim ordinary dividend, other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances was offset by higher Total RWA and on market share buybacks. Total RWA increased by $12.6 billion mainly from higher Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA.
